the css syntax looks right to me, and the stylesheet link in the htm header looks fine too. When I view your page, i see the correct dark purple color. so I think this is a classic example of clearing your cache so your browser reloads the css style rules and isn't using the old one it already saw.

Q: How do I get Qt Designer to find and load Python plugins (on Linux with anaconda)? A: 
I ran into this exact problem a while ago. The issue is that conda-forge builds Python without --enable-shared, so PyQt's build system skips the designer plugin (libpyqt5.so / libpyqt6.so). Without that .so file, Designer has no idea how to talk to Python at all, so PYQTDESIGNERPATH does nothing.

I eventually fixed this for PyQt6 on conda-forge. If you install pyqt6 build _1 (version 6.11.0), you get libpyqt6.so included:

  mamba create -n myenv -c conda-forge "pyqt6=*=*_1" python=3.11 qt6-main
  mamba activate myenv
  designer

It goes in $CONDA_PREFIX/lib/qt6/plugins/designer/libpyqt6.so 

For PyQt5 I haven't done it yet, but honestly Qt5 has been EOL since Dec 2024 so switching to PyQt6 is probably the right call anyway. The API is basically the same.

Q: How can I handle multiple exceptions in Python 3? A:

It may be worth checking out the Errors and Exceptions docs.

In short, you can specify behaviour for different Exception types using the except ExceptionType: syntax where ExceptionType is an Exception derived from the Python Exception class - a list of built-in Python exceptions can be found here.

It is important to note that when an Exception is raised in a try block, Python will execute the code within the first Except block that matches the Exception raised in a top-down manner. For this reason, except Exception: is usually found at the bottom in a given try/except chain as to provide default behaviour for unspecified exceptions that may be raised, it is not first as any Exception raised will trigger this behaviour and thus would make other Except statements within the chain moot.

Example

The below example illustrates the above points.

Here eval() has been used for demonstrative purposes only, please be aware of the inherent dangers of using eval() before you consider using it in your own code.

def demo(e):
    try:
        eval(e)
    except ZeroDivisionError as e:
        print("ZeroDivisionError caught")
        print(e)
    except IndexError as e:
        print("IndexError caught")
        print(e)
    except Exception as e:
        print("Other Exception caught")
        print(e)
    
examples = ["10/0", "[0,1,2][5]", "int('foo')"]

for e in examples:
    demo(e)
    print()

Output

ZeroDivisionError caught
division by zero

IndexError caught
list index out of range

Other Exception caught
invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'foo'

Q: Multiple 'except's with the same code to be executed in Python: If we use logical OR it does not work any idea why? A:

An except clause can take multiple exceptions as a parenthesized tuple, for example

except (FileNotFoundError,ValueError ) as error:
    pass
